newsitem.title: UK: Brazil alcohol plan could still need incentives - Man.
newsitem.headline: Brazil alcohol plan could still need incentives - Man.

text.p: Brazil could implement financial incentives to support its alcohol programme after moving to liberalise the sector earlier this month, trade house E D & F Man said in a report on Tuesday.

In its latest monthly summary, Man noted that Brazil's government had now liberalised anhydrous alcohol while the centre-south growing area expected an increase in cane area of between five and 10 percent.
It did not speculate on what kind of incentives might be introduced.
This had sparked the usual talk of a substantial switch from alcohol to sugar production which could seriously undermine the balance of world sugar supplies.
"It seems, however, that the Brazilian government may introduce a number of taxes/incentives which would continue to support the alcohol programme," Man said.

These included an environmental tax which could in part substitute the current system of alcohol subsidy payment and tax incentives for official transport to encourage the use of alcohol-fuelled vehicles, it said.

Brazil's state oil monopoly Petrobras would cease to be the sole distributor of anhydrous alcohol at officially-set prices from May for centre-south producers and from September for those from the north-east.
Hydrous alcohol prices were set to be liberalised in May 1998 but Petrobras would continue as a distributor.
Man said the 20-percent import tax on alcohol imports had been re-introduced along with tighter restrictions on acceptable import qualities.
"These should unify the rest of the producers and the government in their efforts to secure adequate supplies of alcohol from the domestic cane production," it said.
